ca_zebra_cliffs_north_face.blurb: A shaded wall on the Zebra Cliffs band in the Jumbo Rock part of Joshua Tree National Park. Fifteen short routes, nearly all of them trad cracks and corners with a pair set up for top rope. The grades start around 5.6 and 5.8, then bunch up at 5.10, with a handful of 5.11s as the top end. Because it faces away from the sun it stays comfortable when other Joshua Tree walls are baking, and it is tucked out of sight from the campground side, so it tends to be quiet. Bring a standard trad rack; lines are brief but the cracks are clean.
ca_zebra_cliffs_north_face.parking_note: Leave the car in the G Loop of Jumbo Rocks Campground, then head south on foot.
ca_zebra_cliffs_north_face.approach: Walk roughly half a mile south from the G Loop, up and over a low knoll; the brown cliff band sits on a small plateau on your right.

ca_split_dome_north_rock.blurb: The northern half of Split Dome, a sizeable formation in the Split Rocks group of Joshua Tree's Pinto Basin, split from the southern half by a gully. Fifteen climbs mix trad and sport, running from easy fifth class up to about 5.10d. Expect wide cracks and grainy faces, with the bolted 5.8- face line the area's best known outing. The walk from the lot is almost nothing, making it a quick stop for a few pitches, a warm-up or a day with mixed abilities in the group.

ca_south_horror_rock.blurb: One of the formations nearest the pavement in the Hall of Horrors group, Joshua Tree National Park, reached on a good trail. Fifteen climbs, mostly trad with a few top-rope lines, and a wide spread: a few easy 5.7 to 5.8 climbs, a middle band at 5.9 and 5.10, and several 5.11s and 5.12s for strong leaders. The easiest line is a crack and the most visited, while the harder ones demand balance or steep power. The short walk keeps traffic steady, and the lines sit on the east face.

ca_lower_falls_amphitheater.blurb: A crag on the north side of Yosemite Valley beside Lower Yosemite Falls. Fifteen routes, almost all trad cracks, with a single bolted line. Most of the climbing sits at 5.10 and 5.11, with a 5.6 and a 5.8 for gentler days, plus one route much harder than the rest. Gear lines like Guiding Light and Ten Years After draw most of the attention. It can only be climbed when the creek runs low, and the odd bit of loose rock comes down, so helmets earn their place.

ca_target_rock_sw_face.blurb: A slabby, sunny face on Target Rock in the Oyster Bar area of Joshua Tree National Park, visible from the parking area. Fifteen routes, mostly trad with one sport route and a couple of top-rope setups, running from 5.4 to 5.11a. Most of them are 5.8 and under, so this is a fine place for beginners and for mellow slab days. The face catches afternoon sun, which suits the cooler months, and the shady north face of the same rock sits close by for hot days.
ca_target_rock_sw_face.parking_note: Use the big paved turnout between Ryan Campground and the Hall of Horrors and Saddle Rocks pullouts.
